key_insight: Brain-Adapter combines text-guided and visual multiple-instance learning to classify acute intracranial pathologies from 3D brain CT scans without dense voxel-level annotations.
clinical_relevance: This could make head CT triage and reporting more scalable by helping identify multiple urgent brain abnormalities from routine scans and reports.
method: Uses raw diagnostic sentences as semantic queries in a text-conditioned attention stream.
Runs a parallel visual MIL stream supervised by structured labels extracted with an LLM.
Fuses both streams with an uncertainty-aware refinement module and a consistency constraint.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing the method outperforms state-of-the-art 3D models and standard MIL approaches for scan-level multi-label classification.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of report text, LLM-extracted labels, and external validation across scanners and hospitals before clinical deployment.
paper_title: Brain-Adapter: A Dual-Stream Vision-Language MIL Framework for Comprehensive 3D CT Diagnosis of Acute Intracranial Pathologies
